scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: One cup of coffee, and the sleepiness is gone. Does caffeine give you energy?

scenes.name: adenosine
scenes.text: Not really. As you stay awake, a chemical called adenosine builds up in your brain.

scenes.name: receptors
scenes.text: Adenosine fits into receptors on brain cells, slowing them down, and making you feel tired.

scenes.name: block
scenes.text: Caffeine has a similar shape. It sits in those receptors and blocks adenosine, without slowing anything.

scenes.name: alert
scenes.text: With the brakes off, other brain signals rise, and you feel more alert, within about thirty to sixty minutes.

scenes.name: crash
scenes.text: Adenosine keeps piling up behind the block. When caffeine wears off, the tiredness can hit at once.

scenes.name: halflife
scenes.text: It takes around five hours for half of it to leave your body, so late coffee can mess with sleep.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Not energy, just blocking sleepiness. Follow for more on how things really work.
